text:
Alex: Heads-up — CI is red on the sample-app release branch. Failing integration tests and a regen diff showed up that bumps the client surface (ordering of optional params). Looks like a typegen change slipped through.
Maria: ugh. Which tests? auth retry or parity tests?
Alex: integration tests mostly auth/retry scenarios. sample-app uses token-rotation helper; after regen the SDK now exposes an extra optional param on getToken(), so compiled client snapshot differs.
Jamal: I saw the regen-diff artifact from regen-bot earlier. It flagged a signature reorder in the TypeScript client: `getToken(userId?: string, opts?: GetTokenOptions)` -> `getToken(opts?: GetTokenOptions, userId?: string)`
Olivia: That reordering would be semver-major for our SDK packages. Did typegen add a flag change or is this from OpenAPI input? @regen-bot any clue?
regen-bot: automated-check: regen diff detected in packages/sdk-ts. Diff summary: 1) param reorder in auth client 2) docs updated 3) no new endpoints. CI status: failing on auth integration tests.
Alex: Confirmed. The change came from an OpenAPI refactor where we flattened a schema. Typegen defaulted to a different parameter ordering.
Maria: Can we avoid a breaking release by restoring source-order generation? Maybe a typegen config to preserve original operation order.
Jamal: There's a `--preserve-params` flag in the codegen that we haven't enabled. Quick patch: regenerate with that flag, run `yarn build && yarn test` locally.
Olivia: If we do that, we also need to update changelogs. Right now the release job auto-infers version bump from diffs. If we flip the regen, the inferred semver should go back to patch.
Alex: CI output: ```
FAIL auth-integration › token rotation preserves state
Expected token cache hit, got expired
at tests/auth.test.ts:42
```
Maria: That might be real or a side-effect of the client shape change. Token helper serializes args; if arg order changed, test fixtures pass the wrong param into the helper.
Jamal: Quick repro: run `yarn workspace sample-app test:auth --watch` locally after regen with preserve-params. If fixed, push patch to branch.
Olivia: If we can't flip quickly, another option is to add a compatibility wrapper in the SDK that accepts both orders and maps to current impl. Could be a short-term fix to unblock release.
Alex: I'd prefer regenerating with preserve-params to avoid wrapper technical debt. Who can run regen and kick a patch PR?
Maria: I can run it now. Will do regen, run typecheck, and open PR with `chore(devex): regen with preserve-params to avoid param reorder`
ci-bot: build queued for PR #4821. Full CI will run after push.
Maria: pushed PR. regen-bot reports no diff in public surface now (aside from whitespace). Running `yarn test` locally…
Maria: local tests green for auth integration. Pushing changes.
ci-bot: PR #4821 — build started
Alex: Nice. After CI green, can we also update the release automation to set a hard rule: parameter order changes should be considered breaking unless a config flag indicates deterministic preservation. We keep hitting these surprises.
Jamal: Agreed. I'll file a follow-up RFC about typegen config defaults and add a gating check in the regen CI job to fail if param reorders are detected without an explicit allowlist.
Olivia: Also add a note in the sample-app onboarding doc: "If you regenerate SDKs, prefer `--preserve-params` to avoid breaking test fixtures." Small docs change prevents next person from hitting this.
Alex: Sounds good. Thanks Maria for the fast patch. @regen-bot and ci-bot, thumbs up for the quick feedback loop :thumbsup: 
Maria: np. will merge once CI green and then I'll run the release dry-run to confirm semver inference shows patch.
ci-bot: PR #4821 — build passed
Maria: merged. release-dry-run shows no semver-major inference. rolling out.
Alex: Great. Follow-ups: Jamal to RFC typegen gating, Olivia to update sample-app onboarding, and Maria to monitor canary for auth regressions.
Olivia: noted, adding to my queue.
Jamal: filing RFC now: https://redwood.example.com/rfcs/321-typegen-param-ordering
Alex: closing the loop — thanks everyone.
